record.category: tunnel (hosted): VPN with an anonymous access token, WireGuard and OpenVPN, on shared exit addresses

free_tier.stated: No free tier. The cheapest 1-year token is USD 52: the order page lists 'yearly - $52 (4 devices)' as a PayPal subscription and 'one year - $52 (4 devices)' as a single order; the same page lists 'two years - $94 (5 devices)', 'monthly - $6 (1 device)' and 'weekly - $1.86 (1 device)'.
free_tier.notes: Prices are read from the order forms of the vendor's home page. The FAQ states a device limit that depends on the token's duration: one year gives 4 WireGuard keys and 4 OpenVPN sessions.

retention.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The FAQ states the servers keep no logs that identify a customer; no stored-object retention applies.

egress.terms: No byte cap and no throttling are stated: the FAQ answers 'Are there any speed/traffic limits?' with "No. We don't do any kind of throttling/QoS." Servers are 1 Gbps, and 10 Gbps at five named sites; bandwidth is shared with other servers in the same cabinet.

record.interface_detail: A tunnel, not a data API: OpenVPN (ECC and RSA configurations) and WireGuard, authenticated with a token. Protocols: OpenVPN and WireGuard. UDP: the home page states 'UDP or TCP (1-65535)', so both transports run on any port. Port forwarding: yes, from 30000 to 65535, enabled at http://10.31.33.7/fwd inside the tunnel, 100 forwards per internal IP on each server. SOCKS5 endpoint: unverified: no page read states one. Obfuscation: SSH, HTTPS (Xray or stunnel) and obfs4. BitTorrent: allowed ('BitTorrent allowed').
record.tooling: Any OpenVPN or WireGuard client with the vendor's published server configs; the vendor states all server-side configs are public. Port forwards are made from a web page reachable only inside the tunnel. The vocabulary has no wireguard, openvpn or socks5 interface token, so the interface list says unknown.
record.chaining: A tunnel exit for traffic that must leave from a shared VPN address: a job connects with a token, and the upstream sees one of the provider's shared addresses (over 450 IPs listed).

limits.value: none published: "No. We don't do any kind of throttling/QoS."; servers are 1 Gbps (10 Gbps at Switzerland, Finland, Atlanta, Chicago and Oregon)
shared exit addresses: 'Currently over 450 available IPs', used by many clients at once, so destination-side limits and reputation on an address apply to every client behind it

record.limits_note: Concurrent connections are capped by token length and the vocabulary has no kind for it: a one-week or one-month token allows 1 WireGuard key and 1 OpenVPN session, a one-year token allows 4 and 4, a two-year token 5 and 5, a lifetime token 6 and 6.
record.binding_note: No byte quota, speed cap or request rate is published; the only stated ceiling is the concurrent-session count of the token, which the limit vocabulary cannot name.

identity_cost.detail: A token is the account. The order page's Monero form is labelled 'no 3rd parties, no email or JS required', and the vendor states it accepts Monero 'so people can order an access token anonymously without providing any personal information'. Card and PayPal orders go through PayPal or CCBill, and only recurring subscriptions get the token by email; other orders show it in the browser. The vendor states it has no KYC policy.

record.reliability_note: The FAQ states servers share bandwidth with other servers in the same cabinet, so peak hours can lower speed; port forwards are per server and have to be recreated when moving to another server.
record.confidence_note: Documented: price, protocols, UDP, port forwarding, obfuscation and the BitTorrent line are quoted from the vendor's own home page, FAQ and port-forwarding page. Nothing was connected through the service, so no speed, address class or forwarding behaviour is measured. A SOCKS5 endpoint is unverified because no page read mentions one.
record.price_per_tb_month: USD 52 for a 1-year token (4 devices); a subscription price, not a per-TB price
record.notes: Cheapest yearly price: USD 52 for 1 year, 4 devices (2 years: USD 94, 5 devices). The port-forwarding page says the vendor runs a yearly half-off sale every Black Friday to Cyber Monday; the price above is the list price read on the page.

card.summary: No free tier read. Access is a token bought by duration; the captured pages state no amount, so no price is recorded.

free_tier.stated: No free tier read. Access is a token bought by duration; the captured pages state no amount, so no price is recorded.
free_tier.notes: The price is the vendor's plan rate for the subscription whose exits are classified here; the exit-address measurement itself has no price.

per_object_cap.notes: The classified sample is 36 addresses over 14 ASNs; none of those numbers is an object size.

retention.stated: not applicable: an address, not an object
retention.notes: Nothing is stored, so no retention clock applies. How long one exit address is held before it is re-drawn was not observed.

egress.terms: unverified: no traffic allowance or per-GB price appears in the captured pages; metered is recorded false because no metered charge was read.

record.interface_detail: The server list at https://cryptostorm.is/configs/ is the source of the exit addresses classified here. The schema interface enum has no token for a VPN tunnel, so the tunnel protocols are not recorded as an interface.
record.tooling: The exit addresses are read from https://cryptostorm.is/configs/ and classified with an IP-class detector; the service itself is reached with the vendor's own client or a WireGuard or OpenVPN configuration.
record.chaining: A Worker or a free compute node dials the tunnel and the traffic leaves at one of these exit addresses, so the upstream sees an address in the ASNs listed here and not the caller's network.

limits.value: token duration sets the device limit: a one year token allows 4 WireGuard keys and 4 OpenVPN sessions

record.binding_note: No limit kind binds the record: it measures exit addresses and states no byte quota or request rate. What matters is list membership: 35 of 36 sampled exits are on a datacenter list.

identity_cost.detail: Tokens are delivered in the browser, and only recurring PayPal or CCBill subscribers get a token by email; the FAQ advises cryptocurrency and a disposable email for more anonymity. Whether the purchase form asks for an email is unverified.

record.reliability_note: 35 of 36 sampled exit addresses are on a datacenter list and 23 of 36 on a VPN list, so a site that blocks those lists blocks most of this fleet; 0 of 36 are also on an abuse list.
record.confidence_note: The list membership, ASN spread and counts are measured: each address was answered by the detector at the stated index version. The plan price and the identity class are documented from the vendor's captured pages; where a page did not state them they are unverified. The sample is the addresses the vendor endpoint returned, not proof that every address a user is handed is in it.

evidence.proved: The vendor endpoint https://cryptostorm.is/configs/ gave 36 IPv4 exit addresses, each answered by the address-class detector at index version 20261103T163900Z-00d117b2 on 2026-11-03. Datacenter list: 35 of 36; VPN list: 23 of 36 (23 in the x4b VPN list); abuse list: 0 of 36; on none of the three: 1 of 36. 14 distinct ASNs and 36 distinct /24s; largest ASN AS9009 M247 M247 Europe SRL with 23 addresses.
Detector index version 20261103T163900Z-00d117b2 was the one every one of the 36 answers carries.
token duration sets the device limit; a one year token allows 4 WireGuard keys and 4 OpenVPN sessions

evidence.quote: Around February of 2024 we changed the delivery setup where now only people who have a recurring subscription (via PayPal or CCBill) get their tokens delivered by email.
evidence.proved: the token is delivered in the browser unless the buyer holds a recurring subscription

record.notes: List membership of 36 exit addresses (detector index version 20261103T163900Z-00d117b2, 2026-11-03): datacenter 35, VPN 23, abuse 0, none of the three 1. VPN list: 23 of 36, of which 23 are in the x4b VPN list. Definitions: datacenter is an address inside a range the x4b datacenter list publishes; VPN is inside the x4b VPN list or a per-provider server list; abuse is on at least one independent abuse family; none of the three states list membership, not physical siting.

extras.rung_note: Addresses came from the vendor's own server list and each was classified; no exit was connected to, so the address a user is handed at connect time was not observed.
